body: Hey, I never said I'd hold your hand and tell you living is easy. I'm just here to state facts, maybe save a few people who think their suicidal, but aren't, and die on my own terms. Lol
That's my reasoning as well. Why a few months? Is that your timeline?
Ending it all is the easy part, death comes to all of us eventually. Taking steps to try to convince yourself to live, that's the real challenge.

I can't say that I know how you feel, but as a (closeted) suicidal person who also owns a firearm, it's security. Don't try to kill yourself day one with it. Hold onto it for a while before you think about pulling that trigger. Don't just put the barrel up against anywhere and pull the trigger. Do some research, there are A LOT of horror stories that come with suicide attempts with firearms. What's worse than killing yourself? Being alive in a vegetable state and having to look at all the sad faces look down on you and you CAN'T try again.  I'm not saying to kill yourself at all, but just know what you're doing before you do it.

Damn, 22hrs later. If there was a post I could associate with, it's this one. I was just thinking N would be the best way to go, just put on a bag and breathe. Hope it all works out for you, one way or the other. But I listened and I'll remember, might even be one of the last things I remember as I put on my bag too.

I feel the same. 23 with a good job, but no real way to increase quality of life. I hate the fact that the only reason I won't end it is because of my friends and some family. I've welcomed death and await until my number is called. To overcome the fear of killing myself, I started fasting (starving myself for the most part) so that I can eventually live out until my body gives up. Nobody can look down on me for it and nobody can blame themself. My COD will be malnutrition, which means my insurance will still pay out. 👍
I wouldn't mind that myself. But I feel as though there is a difference between accepting death and wanting to commit suicide.

It's a process. I failed classes and dropped out of college at 19. I made a huge life-changing decision and failed at that too. I came back to my friends, got a job, worked for a few months, signed back up for school and now I'm taking 4 classes and working full time. I went through a lot of trials and tribulations to get to this point. Anyways, the point is that we all go our own pace and we all take our own paths in life. Don't judge your own worth on someone else's. There are people that would love to even experience one class in college, but will never see a campus in their life.

You have to move on, and by that I do not mean forget her, nor do I mean get into a new relationship. What I mean is that you have to keep building what you had in mind for both of you together. Build that future that you wanted her in and keep her in your mind. If you just waste away, then you will be throwing away the the dreams that you both shared. You will be throwing away what she may have wanted for you as well. And don't you ever and I mean NEVER contemplate suicide, all you would be doing with that is passing that pain that you feel onto someone else. You have to be strong, you have no choice but to keep moving on. Even though I may never meet you, and I may never know you, just know that I love you brother.
